key_insight: Bag-of-waves learns a compact, human-interpretable dictionary of recurring EEG waveforms instead of relying on fixed handcrafted features or opaque deep models. This makes EEG analysis more explainable and better suited to low-data settings.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the tradeoff between interpretability and performance in EEG analysis, especially when labeled data are scarce. It aims to replace rigid predefined spectral features and data-hungry deep networks with a learnable, understandable representation.
method: Learn a small dictionary of recurring EEG waveform patterns from data.
Represent each EEG signal as a bag of these learned waves, capturing spatial and temporal structure.
Use the learned waveform tokens for downstream evaluation tasks in low-data regimes while keeping the model interpretable.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path to interpretable biomarker discovery without requiring large datasets or heavy compute. It is especially relevant for biomedical applications where transparency and data efficiency matter.

paper_title: Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes
paper_authors: Athanasios Papastathopoulos-Katsaros, Steven T. Lee, Lin Yao, Ajay Thomas, Junseok Park
